claim: The next round has two tasks, and the round after it has one. Round 7 decides the four-set cubic identity on the equality margin (26, 338, 5), and it tests one 5-regular tournament on 11 vertices that keeps the J=5, s=4 counts and keeps every pair of zero-excess vertices at most 3 common in-neighbours. Round 8 runs the pair and triple identities at J=5 and s=5. The bound f(4) >= 52 stays checked, the bound f(4) <= 67 stays unchanged, the pair and triple moments stay compatible with every triple having at least 5 dominators, and three-level deletion stays closed. Erdős problem 902 is not solved.
definitions: S_4 means every 4-set has a dominator outside itself. f(4) is the least order of a tournament with S_4. A pair is tight when it has exactly 11 dominators. For a tight pair, J is the sum of (in-degree minus 25) over those 11 dominators, and s is the number of those dominators whose in-degree is greater than 25. The equality margin (26, 338, 5) is the degree pattern of twenty-six in-degrees 25 and twenty-six in-degrees 26, pair excesses summing to 338, and triple dominator counts tested at 5. A zero-excess dominator is one of the seven vertices of in-degree 25 in the J=5, s=4 pattern. The four-set cubic identity is sum over 4-sets of C(|D(X)|, 3) = sum over triples of C(ν(Y), 4), where ν(Y) is the number of common out-neighbours of the triple. A strategy is an allocation of tasks, not a theorem.
argument:
Settled inputs, left closed. f(4) >= 52 is the checked bound in research/LEMMAS.md. f(4) <= 67 is the Paley tournament of order 67, and the explicit families of orders 52 through 66 in R4-D do not improve it. Lemma S1, R4-B, and R5-B give the equality margin an integer solution in which every triple has at least 5 dominators and the transitive dominator sum is 91572. R4-G forces some triple to have at least 7 dominators under the triple hypothesis and does not remove that solution. R5-G and the on-disk report R6-G keep a second score sequence alive as integers: the extreme sequence meets sum C(ν, 2) = 388592 and the third-moment symmetry with every dominator count at least 5. R5-F shows that three nested deletions leave the coefficient of log2 log2 N equal to 1, and that a further deletion of the same kind has the same shape. That approach key is exhausted.

What those inputs do not decide. An S_4 tournament on 52 vertices is still open, so f(4) is still only pinned between 52 and 67. The no-tight branch and the tight-pair branch are separate. On the no-tight branch, R6-B, read from disk, records that the pair and triple identities do not contradict S_4. The four-set count sum |D(X)| = sum_v C(d^+(v), 4) is at least 717600 against C(52, 4) = 270725, and on the equality margin the second-moment companion is at least 730730 and still allows every 4-set two dominators. The identity those two comparisons leave open is the four-set cubic. On the tight-pair branch, R4-C leaves one pattern at J=5 and s=4, with positive counts 16, 14, 13, 13, 12, 12 and common-in-neighbour numbers 4, 3, 2, 2, 3, 0. R5-C realises those six numbers in one 5-regular tournament on vertices 0 through 10. R6-C, read from disk, shows that the two heavy vertices cannot sit against that tournament: the zero-excess pair {6, 9} has four common in-neighbours, and the pair-excess budget at either endpoint is 10 against a lower bound of 14. The same report says a different tournament, with every zero-excess pair at most 3, is not excluded. At J=5 the conditional bound s >= 4 leaves two degree shapes. Four positive excesses sum to 5 only as 2, 1, 1, 1, which is the shape already under test. Five positive excesses sum to 5 only as 1, 1, 1, 1, 1. Six or more positive integers cannot sum to 5. The identities at s=5 have not been run.

Allocation. Round 7 spends one task on each branch that a proof of no S_4 tournament on 52 vertices has to close, at the first identity the latest report leaves open. The cubic task asks whether the repaired rows of R5-B can sit under the four-set cubic with every 4-set dominated. It takes as input the fact that the pair and triple moments do not force a triple below 5, and it does not try to force that triple bound again. The tournament task asks for one 5-regular tournament on 11 vertices with the six positive counts, with every common-in-neighbour count from the four positive vertices into the seven at most 3, and with every pair inside the seven at most 3, and then applies the same heavy-vertex budget. A counting proof that no such tournament exists is a valid result. A list of the isomorphism classes of the regular tournaments on 11 vertices is not. Round 8 runs the s=5 shape. It is the other half of J=5 once s >= 4 is granted, and it can be specified before the round-7 tournament returns. The two round-7 tasks are on different branches, so they can run together. The s=5 task is the next tight-pair shape, sequenced one round later so that the live s=4 obstruction is the tight-pair task in the nearer round.

Left outside these three slots. The extreme score sequence now has integer rows meeting the dominated-side moments. One surviving margin already shows that those moments do not force a triple below 5, so the intersection test named in R6-G is the reserve behind the cubic, for a later round if the cubic still allows every 4-set a dominator. J >= 6 remains after J=5. A further deletion level has the shape already computed in R5-F. Another explicit family in orders 52 through 66 is the continuation of a census that left f(4) <= 67 unchanged. The checked bound f(4) >= 52 is not reopened. None of the three tasks declares Erdős problem 902 solved.

round_7_tasks.target: Use the repaired (k, ν) rows in research/AGENT_TASKS/R5-B-outsets.report.json. They meet every triple at least 5 dominators, the transitive dominator sum 91572, and the pair and third moments on the equality margin. research/AGENT_TASKS/R6-B-s4.report.json records that sum |D(X)| = sum_v C(d^+(v), 4) is at least 717600 against 270725 four-sets, and that sum C(|D(X)|, 2) = sum_P C(μ(P), 4) is at least 730730 and still allows every 4-set two dominators. Decide sum over 4-sets of C(|D(X)|, 3) = sum over triples of C(ν(Y), 4) on those rows. Either give nonnegative four-set counts, every |D(X)| at least 1, meeting this equation together with the two earlier four-set equations, or prove that no such counts exist. If another ν distribution meets the same triple equations and changes the verdict, record that distribution. Keep the pair and triple solution as an input.

weaknesses: This is a strategy. It proves no bound and it exhibits no tournament. The three round-6 reports were read from disk and are not yet ledger entries. J >= 5 and s >= 4 remain conditional on unreviewed reports in the same agent line. A four-set solution on the equality margin leaves the extreme score sequence untouched, and an exclusion on that margin leaves every other score sequence untouched. One 11-vertex tournament can meet the zero-excess condition and still reject the two heavy vertices, and acceptance of those two vertices would leave the 37 light vertices unassigned. A proof that no such tournament exists does not by itself close J=5 and s=4. The s=5 task does not treat J >= 6. Erdős problem 902 is not solved, and these three tasks do not determine f(4).
